title: Notification bubbles are stacked improperly when more appear in quick succession than can fit on the screen at once
line: When many notifications arrive at once, the ones that don't fit wait their turn instead of appearing alone at the top of the screen.
explanation: positionPopups() places popups and hides any that would fill more than 80% of the screen. But when a popup was created, the applet called positionPopups() and then set the popup visible unconditionally, overriding that decision. In a burst, a popup created while the others were still being sized could end up shown far above the stack, at the top edge of the screen. The change drops the unconditional show, so positionPopups() alone decides which popups are visible.

commits.message:
applets/notifications: Don't show popups that don't fit on screen

positionPopups() hides popups past the part of the screen they may fill,
but each new popup was then made visible anyway, so a burst of them put
extra popups far above the stack; leave visibility to positionPopups().

BUG: 510647

media.caption: Master: 50 notify-send calls; popups 1-7 stacked, then a gap and popup 11 alone at the top edge
Fixed: same 50 calls; popups 1-7 stacked evenly, nothing shown above them
Fixed: after the first batch closes, the waiting popups (8-14) take their place, evenly spaced

review.text: Removing the unconditional object.visible = true lets positionPopups() be the only place that decides visibility, which is what it was designed for. The fix is minimal and the screenshots show the stray top popup gone and the queued popups coming in evenly.
